content: The image description page is divided into four distinct sections. For an image, these sections include: 1. The image itself. 2. A detailed description of the image or sound. 3. A section labeled Image history. 4. A section labeled Image links or File links. For images hosted on Wikimedia Commons, the local image page will display the following elements: 1. The image itself. 2. A message related to the image. 3. Local editable content specific to the image. 4. Editable content from Wikimedia Commons, which may include transcluded content from other Commons pages. These sections are not numbered and do not appear in the table of contents (TOC). 5. A list of local pages that utilize the image. The description section of the page also has an edit history, which is labeled as Image: xxx Revision history. This label can be somewhat confusing and should not be mistaken for the Image history section. The following information pertains specifically to the description section, with a particular focus on images. Useful Information to Include on an Image Description Page The description section of the page allows for the inclusion of text. Initially, this section automatically contains the upload summary provided by the user when the first version of the image was uploaded. This text also appears in the Image history section under the first upload entry. Description of the Image For example: Image of a goldfish in a small tank. This description should not serve as alternative text but rather as a clear and concise explanation of the image. This is particularly useful for users who do not have direct access to the image and serves as a temporary substitute for a proper long description tag. You may also include the dimensions of the image, expressed in pixels. All information provided on this page is attributed to WikiDoc.
